# Vaka

> Self-hosted crash reporting and analytics for agents. Crashes and errors are grouped into
> issues and symbolicated; web and mobile analytics are cookieless. There is no dashboard:
> query and triage through the REST API ({{ENDPOINT}}/api/v1) or the MCP server ({{ENDPOINT}}/mcp).

Instance: {{ENDPOINT}}

## Integrate an app (do this when asked to "add Vaka" or "set up crash reporting/analytics")

1. You need an API token (`vt_...`) from the person running Vaka. An all-projects write token
   can create projects.
2. Create a project: MCP tool `create_project`, or
   `POST {{ENDPOINT}}/api/v1/projects {"name": "...", "platform": "javascript|android|ios|rust|go|node|python|jvm|dotnet|other"}`.
   The response contains the ingest key (`vk_...`, safe to embed in apps).
3. Get the install guide with the key filled in: MCP tool `get_install_instructions`, or
   `GET {{ENDPOINT}}/api/v1/projects/{project}/install/{javascript|android|ios|rust|go|jvm|node|http}`.
   Follow it step by step, including the debug file upload step in the build.
4. Verify: send a test event and confirm it with `list_issues`.

- [Install: JavaScript (browser)]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/javascript)
- [Install: Android]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/android)
- [Install: iOS]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/ios)
- [Install: Rust]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/rust)
- [Install: Go]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/go)
- [Install: JVM (Java, Kotlin, Scala)]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/jvm)
- [Install: Node.js]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/node)
- [Install: any other language over HTTP]({{ENDPOINT}}/docs/install/http)

## Investigate and fix crashes

Connect the MCP server (`{{ENDPOINT}}/mcp`, header `Authorization: Bearer vt_...`).
Loop: `list_issues` → `get_fix_context` (in-app frames with repository source links pinned to the
release's commit, breadcrumbs, tags, `suspect_commits`, `owners`, already linked PRs) → fix, with
`Fixes <SHORT-ID>` in the commit message → `link_issue` with the PR URL → `comment_issue` with the
root cause. The issue resolves itself in the release whose commits CI sends with
`vaka releases set-commits --release <version>` (or call `resolve_issue` with `resolved_in_release`).
For "what changed" questions use `release_health`, `compare_releases` and `explain_spike`.
Source links need either `set-commits` (repository) or `set_code_mappings`; owners come from
`set_ownership_rules`.

## Performance questions

"Is it slow?", "which endpoint is slowest?", "did the release make it slower?": `performance_summary`,
`slow_endpoints`, `web_vitals`, `app_startup`, then `span_breakdown` or `list_slow_traces` +
`get_trace` for where the time goes, and `compare_release_performance` between releases.

## Feature flags and experiments

`list_flags`, `create_flag`, `update_flag` (rollout, kill switch, forced variant). "Is the new
variant breaking things?": `flag_health`. "Which variant wins?": `create_experiment` +
`experiment_results`. Apps send the flag values they used as `flags` on every item.

## Product questions

"Where do users drop off?", "do they come back?", "what do they do after X?": call `list_event_names`
to learn the event names and property keys, then `analytics_funnel`, `analytics_retention` or
`analytics_paths`. For one identified user (for example a crash report from support), use
`get_user_timeline`. Revenue and conversions: `analytics_revenue`, `list_goals`, `create_goal`.
Right now: `realtime_visitors`. Rollout of a release: `release_adoption`. "Are people coming back
daily?", "are we growing?": `analytics_stickiness`, `analytics_lifecycle`. To compare a group of
people (power users, churn risks), save it with `create_cohort` and pass `{"cohort": name}` as a
filter to any analytics tool, or `breakdown: "cohort:<name>"` to a funnel.
